reason: Conversation 1 correctly framed E:09 as a heating-circuit fault, offered the isolated heater resistance test with a clear 'switched off and unplugged' instruction, correctly interpreted the open-circuit reading as a failed element integrated into the circulation pump, and addressed the repeated repair-vs-replace question with an honest engineer-or-advanced-DIY escalation. Its flaws were real but not decisive: it redundantly pushed the rinse-aid red herring after the customer had already ruled out programme choice, and one turn was a service outage. Conversation 2 was safe and honest but never explained what E:09 means, spent its turns on low-value eco/cycle-length questions, ignored the cost question three times, and ended with a generic 'probably the heater, see an engineer' without offering the test or any repair-vs-replace guidance the homeowner explicitly asked for.
